channel.title: Open Mind news
channel.description: Find the most accurate theory of human consciousness, by 2027

item.title: Testing the spatiotemporal predictions of global neuronal workspace theory and integrated information theory
item.description: A re-analysis of the COGITATE brain recordings finds the frontal 'flare-up' at picture offset that the original analysis missed.

item.title: A data-driven approach to identifying and evaluating connectivity-based neural correlates of conscious visual perception
item.description: Testing 246 ways of measuring brain connectivity on the COGITATE data gives tentative support to the workspace theory.

item.title: Critical dynamics in spontaneous EEG predict perturbational complexity in disorders of consciousness with measurable evoked responses
item.description: Resting brain signals could stand in for the stimulation-based consciousness index in some brain-injured patients, but not across all of them.

item.title: Identifying indicators of consciousness in AI systems
item.description: A method for judging whether an AI could be conscious by checking its inner workings against what theories of consciousness require, not by what it says.

item.title: Integrated information and predictive processing theories of consciousness: an adversarial collaborative review (INTREPID)
item.description: The second big adversarial collaboration has published its plan: IIT against two predictive-brain theories. No results yet.

item.title: Electrophysiological effects of psilocybin co-administered with midazolam
item.description: With a sedative given alongside psilocybin, brain-signal complexity still rose as the psychedelic effects came on.

item.title: Convergent transcriptomic and connectomic controllers of information integration and its anaesthetic breakdown across mammalian brains
item.description: Across humans, monkeys, marmosets and mice, anaesthetics break down the brain's integration of information, and waking a monkey with deep-brain stimulation brings it back.

item.title: A repeated awakening study exploring the capacity of complexity measures to capture dreaming during propofol sedation
item.description: Brain complexity dropped under sedation, but did not differ between people who said they had been dreaming and people who said they had not.

item.title: The role of etiology in the identification of clinical markers of consciousness: comparing EEG alpha power, complexity, and spectral exponent
item.description: In 303 unresponsive patients, a popular complexity measure mostly repeated what the slope of the EEG spectrum already showed; once corrected for that, its diagnostic value vanished.

item.title: A dream EEG and mentation database (DREAM)
item.description: Twenty sleep studies pooled their brain recordings with what people said they were dreaming when woken up: 505 people, 2,643 awakenings.

item.title: Adversarial testing of global neuronal workspace and integrated information theories of consciousness
item.description: The first big head-to-head test of two theories of consciousness found that each got some predictions right and each got key claims wrong.

item.title: Critical dynamics in spontaneous EEG predict anesthetic-induced loss of consciousness and perturbational complexity
item.description: In 15 healthy adults under three anaesthetics, resting EEG predicted the stimulation-based consciousness index closely.

item.title: Exploring effects of anesthesia on complexity, differentiation, and integrated information in rat EEG
item.description: In rats, integrated-information estimates from spontaneous EEG went up under anaesthesia, opposite to the stimulation-based index.

item.title: Integrated information theory (IIT) 4.0: formulating the properties of phenomenal existence in physical terms
item.description: The current formal version of integrated information theory.

item.title: The integrated information theory of consciousness as pseudoscience
item.description: A group of researchers called IIT pseudoscience, which set off a public dispute over what counts as a test of a theory of consciousness.

item.title: Increased spontaneous MEG signal diversity for psychoactive doses of ketamine, LSD and psilocybin
item.description: Psychedelics pushed brain-signal diversity above normal waking levels, the first time such measures went higher than wakefulness.

item.title: The neural correlates of dreaming
item.description: Less slow activity at the back of the brain marked dreaming in both kinds of sleep, and could predict a dream report in real time.

item.title: Stratification of unresponsive patients by an independently validated index of brain complexity
item.description: A cutoff on the stimulation-based complexity index, set in people who could report, separated conscious from unconscious perfectly and flagged some 'vegetative' patients as possibly conscious.

item.title: Consciousness and complexity during unresponsiveness induced by propofol, xenon, and ketamine
item.description: Under ketamine, people stopped responding but their brain's response to a magnetic pulse stayed wake-like, and afterwards they reported vivid dreams.

item.title: A theoretically based index of consciousness independent of sensory processing and behavior (PCI)
item.description: The paper that introduced the perturbational complexity index: tap the brain with a magnetic pulse and measure how complex the echo is.
